title: Granting that, whether original righteousness is called natural or supernatural matters less, if it is God's free gift
source_text: LI. Hoc autem semel concesso, fieri non posse ut homo a Deo creetur absque justitia & sanctitate, tanti momenti non videtur altera illa quaestio. An Justitia & Sanctitas illa in qua Deus primum hominem condidit, & sine qua creari a Deo non potuit, pertineat ad naturae, vel ad gratiae dotes, & naturalis dicenda sit, vel supernaturalis: Modo, quod omnes concedunt, statuamus illam esse gratuitum Dei donum, quod nullis creaturae meritis debebatur.
pass_a_gloss: But this being once granted, that it cannot happen that man be created by God without justice and sanctity, that other question does not seem of so great moment. Whether that Justice and Sanctity in which God founded the first man, and without which he could not be created by God, pertains to the endowments of nature, or of grace, and is to be called natural, or supernatural: Provided, what all grant, we hold that it is a gratuitous gift of God, which was owed to no merits of the creature.
pass_b_english: Once it is granted that God cannot create man without righteousness and holiness, the other question does not seem so important: whether the righteousness and holiness in which God made the first man, and without which God could not have created him, belongs to the endowments of nature or of grace, and should be called natural or supernatural. That holds provided we affirm, as everyone grants, that it is God's free gift, owed to no merit of the creature.

choices.why: Modo with the subjunctive is a proviso; Le Blanc's irenic point depends on it.
